scope: Whole Federer 3.2.30, p. 268: both linear exterior-diameter and Hausdorff image bounds hold for every positive integer degree and arbitrary source sets, with the actual exterior operator norm. No measurability, boundedness, finite-mass or source/target degree-bound premise is imposed.
proof_route: The actual exterior functor and operator norm control endpoint words. Independent supremum laws give the exterior diameter and shared normalization gives the cost bound. The finite ordinary linear norm supplies a positive Lipschitz cutoff factor. Positive exterior norm permits the existing scaled Caratheodory transport. At zero exterior norm, every nonempty image generator has zero actual cost; a countable small-diameter cover of the Euclidean source gives zero image mass at every positive target cutoff, including unbounded sources. The independent H<=S, 2.10.39 and T<=H comparisons then give the printed Hausdorff coefficient.
source_conventions: Euclidean spaces use the coordinate models of the public metric-measure interfaces. The dimension coefficient n^(k/2) is sqrt(n)^k. Supporting cost and exterior-image lemmas also allow degree zero; the numbered theorem retains positive degree. The displayed product uses the existing extended-nonnegative zero-times-infinity convention; zero-norm image nullity is proved directly from covers. No new erratum correction or changed positive-degree statement.
coverage_qualification: Retain the source corrections of 3.2.27 and 3.2.29 and the deferred 2.10.46. Items 3.2.31–3.2.49 remain pending; unregistered item31 supporting drafts are not certified by this release.
